I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep doing what is most steady and familiar for my land and my age: the main pattern will be winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the safest way for me to use the full year, match the local weather, and rely on work I already know well. I am 72, so I do not want crops that need too much fine management or too much market gambling. Wheat and maize both have stable local experience, easy access to seed, fertilizer, irrigation, and machine services. I will mostly use improved or hybrid seed, because I want reliable emergence and yield, but I will not choose anything too complicated.

For management, I will keep the field work simple. For wheat, I will use ploughing before sowing if the land needs turning, apply base fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize so I do not lose moisture or time. For maize, I will use rotary tillage or light preparation, put fertilizer in a simple way, irrigate only when needed, and keep pesticide use limited to the main pest periods. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because at my age I value steady work, lower labor pressure, and harvest I can count on.
